To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the consumption of a whey protein drink, containing specific amino acids, prior to a composite meal significantly reduced postprandial glucose response, in absence of a significant increase in insulinemia.
pre-meal drinks with protein or amino acids reduce glycemia at a subsequent meal in healthy individuals.
a pre-mealing drink containing specific proteins and amino acids can reduce postprandial glucose excursions following a composite meal without elevating insulinemic responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of pre-meal drinks with protein and amino acids on glycemic and metabolic responses at a subsequent composite (real food) meal.
the effect of protein and amino acid drinks served prior to a composite meal on postprandial glucose and insulin responses.
the effects of specific pre-meal drinks with protein and amino acids on glycemia, insulinemia, incretins, and subjective appetite in healthy volunteers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a pre-mealing bolus of whey protein, with or without amino acids, reduces postprandia glycemia in absence of elevated plasma insulin levels.
pre-meal drinks with whey proteins, or with specific mixtures of amino acids, reduce postprandial glucose responses following a subsequent meal.
pre-meal drinks containing specific proteins or amino acids significantly reduces post-prandial glycemia in healthy subjects following a composite meal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pre-meal drink significantly lowered the postprandial glucose response, in absence of increased insulinemic excursions, and that an early phase insulinemic effect induced by plasma amino acid and incretin concentrations appears to mediate this effect.
a pre-meals with whey protein and specific amino acids, in absence of carbohydrates, reduces glycemia and the glucose peak following a composite meal.

a pre-meals drink with whey protein and specific amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, lysine, threonine, and valine) reduces the glycemic response at a subsequent composite test meal, in absence to elevated insulin excursions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a pre-mealing drink containing protein and/or specific amino acids, can reduce the glycemic and insulin response to a meal.
the pre-meal drink with whey protein and specific amino acids can significantly reduce postprandial glucose excursions following a composite meal.
pre-meal drinks containing whey proteins and amino acids reduce postprandial glucose responses following a composite meal.
